newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SEEN ON COURSE FOR MILLION NEW HOMES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SEEN ON COURSE FOR MILLION NEW HOMES.

text.p: South Africa's programme to build one million homes for the poor by the end of the century has gone too slowly but is still on course, Housing Minister Sankie Mthembi-Nkondo said on Thursday.
"Housing delivery has been moving at a pace which is slower than desirable," she told a news briefing at the start of the 1997 parliamentary session.

Mthembo-Nkondo said there had been a lack of skills in town planning and construction when President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress launched its bid to house the country's black masses after winning historic all-race elections in April 1994.
"We don't have enough programme managers, we don't have administrators, we don't have accountants," she said.
The government plans to provide housing subsidies of 15,000 rand ($3,400) to 400,000 people earning less than 3,500 rand a month by mid-1999.
But the slow pace of housing construction has been a recurring criticism of the ANC government over the last two years.

"There's been a lot of improvement," Mthembo-Nkondo said. "By 1999, we will have built, or will have projects under construction, that mean we will be able to meet our targetted promise when this government took over in 1994."
She said her ministry was targetting people with incomes of less than 1,000 rand a month, who she said made up 49 percent of the total population of around 42 million.
